mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market, driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic growth, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the quarters with positive GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate increased economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and CPI inflation rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates tightening monetary conditions, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs and reduced consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate increased consumer spending and economic growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales over two consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate increased corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the months with positive retail and food services sales growth.
